notes: Two articles queued, both read, both naming an address.

findings.description: The Planning Department approved in July a three-story, roughly 31-foot residential infill at 720 Masonic Avenue — two four-bedroom apartments and a two-bedroom ADU — replacing the site of the December 2023 three-alarm fire that destroyed the house there and displaced seven residents. Xie Associates filed the application. The gutted structure was demolished in 2024 and the vacant parcel sold for $1.35 million in 2023. No building stands there yet, so the building block stays empty.

extra.proposed_use: two four-bedroom apartments, one two-bedroom ADU

citation.label: Hoodline, “NoPa Lot Scarred by 2023 Fire Set to Rise Again as Three-Story Infill,” 24 September 2026

raw.text: the San Francisco Planning Department signing off in July on a three-story residential infill to replace the site of a devastating 2023 fire

resolution.method: EAS exact match on 720 MASONIC AVE → parcel 1197085; sf-parcels has blklot 1197085 active, 720–720 MASONIC; the 2025 roll records it as single family residential, built 1912. EAS puts 720, 722 MASONIC AVE on that parcel, so per the directory contract the fact belongs on one page at the lowest, 720. EAS files the address under parcel 1197021, which sf-parcels reports retired; the active parcel its coordinates fall in is 1197085.

publish.note: One event, one entry. /san-francisco/castro/masonic-avenue/720/ already carries this planning approval as 'New Building Permits For 720 Masonic Avenue in NoPa, San Francisco,' San Francisco YIMBY, 2026-09-23. Hoodline's account the next day adds no new fact — the applicant, height and unit mix are the same story — so nothing here changes the page.

findings.description: A permit application, per San Francisco YIMBY, seeks to demolish the single-family house at 768 De Haro Street and replace it with a curved, roughly 40-foot building holding a primary residence and a studio apartment, designed by Stanley Saitowitz of Natoma Architects. The property last sold in April for $2 million. No building matching the design exists yet, so the building block stays empty for the design team.

citation.label: Hoodline, “Potrero Hill Owners Pitch Curved 40-Foot House to Replace $2M Teardown,” 23 September 2026

raw.text: the permit application seeks to replace the existing single-family house with a primary residence and studio apartment

resolution.method: EAS exact match on 768 DE HARO ST → parcel 4072007; sf-parcels has blklot 4072007 active, 768–768 DE HARO; the 2025 roll records it as single family residential, built 1908.

publish.note: One event, one entry. /san-francisco/potrero-hill/de-haro-street/768/ already carries this permit filing as 'Permits Filed For Rounded House at 768 De Haro Street, Potrero Hill, San Francisco,' San Francisco YIMBY, 2026-09-23 — the same source (SF YIMBY) Hoodline itself cites. Nothing here adds a fact the page doesn't already have.
